ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Mahalia Jackson — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Nine weeks of treatment: lung function, calcium, methotrexate safety, the new defibrillator, steroid effects, and her concert schedule

text.paragraph: Review after nine weeks of treatment. [S]

Ms. Jackson returns nine weeks after starting prednisone and methotrexate. The electrophysiology study induced sustained ventricular tachycardia, and a dual-chamber defibrillator was placed the next day; the wound has healed and she has had no shocks. The remote transmission last week showed two short runs of ventricular tachycardia in March and none since. She climbs two flights before stopping, the cough has gone, and the palpitations are rare. She has had a large appetite, gained weight, and sleeps poorly on prednisone. Home glucose readings are 100 to 130 mg/dL. She has had no mouth sores, nausea or infections on methotrexate, and drinks no alcohol. The final EBUS cultures were negative. No methotrexate blood tests have been done since she started. She is eager to sing again and has concerts offered from the end of May. She has had no thoughts of self-harm. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1964-05-11; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 94.0 kg; blood pressure 138/86, pulse 66 and regular
Regular rhythm; no murmur; defibrillator pocket healed without swelling or tenderness
Mild facial fullness; no bruising or infection

Breathlessness on exertion and a dry cough for three months, worse on tour, with tiredness and chest tightness; she can no longer hold long phrases; bilateral hilar lymph node enlargement on today's chest radiograph; granulomas were reported at an abdominal operation twelve years ago, with no pathology report available: sarcoidosis must be confirmed by tissue and other causes excluded
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to the documented breathlessness during performances and the 1952 granulomas. Superseded by the tissue diagnosis at the consultation.

Palpitations with two spells of light-headedness while singing; ECG today: sinus rhythm with first-degree atrioventricular block (PR 240 ms) and frequent ventricular ectopic beats: cardiac involvement must be looked for
S — Synthetic finding; superseded when cardiac sarcoidosis was diagnosed.
Hypercalcemia: calcium 10.8 mg/dL with a high 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D and a low 25-hydroxyvitamin D, while taking an over-the-counter calcium and vitamin D supplement; creatinine slightly raised
S — Synthetic finding; resolved on treatment.

Pulmonary sarcoidosis with hilar and mediastinal lymph node involvement (Scadding stage II), confirmed by non-necrotizing granulomas on EBUS-guided lymph node aspiration with negative stains and cultures; mild restriction and reduced diffusing capacity; synthetic modern detail linked to her documented sarcoidosis
S — Synthetic histology, stage and lung function; her biographer reports a diagnosis of sarcoidosis after granulomas were found at an operation (D, probable).

Cardiac sarcoidosis: first-degree atrioventricular block, ventricular ectopy (6 percent of beats) with nonsustained ventricular tachycardia, left ventricular ejection fraction 47 percent, patchy late gadolinium enhancement of the basal septum and inferolateral wall, and matching focal FDG uptake on PET; synthetic modern detail linked to the documented private account that sarcoidosis was in her heart
S — Synthetic cardiac findings; the account that her doctors told her sarcoidosis was in her heart rests on her biographer (D, probable), and the interpretation of her later heart disease is R.
Long-term systemic glucocorticoid treatment for sarcoidosis, with bone, glucose, blood pressure, infection and eye risks to manage
Dual-chamber implantable cardioverter-defibrillator, placed after sustained monomorphic ventricular tachycardia was induced at electrophysiology study; remote monitoring
S — Synthetic device status after the synthetic implant.

list.item:
Cardiac sarcoidosis on treatment, with a defibrillator (D86.85). Clinically better: rare palpitations, no ventricular tachycardia since March, NT-proBNP 140 pg/mL from 240. The defibrillator protects her against sudden death while the inflammation settles. [S]
Prednisone taper: 30 mg daily for four weeks, then 20 mg for four weeks, 15 mg for four weeks, and 10 mg until the review in August.
Methotrexate increased to 20 mg once weekly.
Continue metoprolol; monthly remote device checks; clinic device check in three months.
Repeat FDG-PET and echocardiogram in mid-August.

Implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (Z95.810). Wound healed; she may drive again and lift her left arm fully. Singing and stage movement are safe; she should keep mobile phones and headphones 15 cm from the device and walk through airport security with her device card. [S]
Device card and travel letter given.
Remote monitor travels with her.

Pulmonary sarcoidosis (D86.2). Lung function improving: FVC 84 percent from 74, DLCO 70 percent from 62. [S]
Repeat lung function in August.

Hypercalcemia (E83.52). Calcium 9.6 mg/dL, normal on prednisone; resolved. Vitamin D can now be replaced cautiously: 25-hydroxyvitamin D 24 ng/mL. [S]
Cholecalciferol 1000 units daily, with calcium at the next visit.
Problem resolved.

Long-term systemic glucocorticoid treatment (Z79.52). Steroid effects: blood pressure 138/86, glucose 118 mg/dL and A1c 6.3% (from 5.9%), weight up 2.8 kg, poor sleep. Bone density in March showed moderate fracture risk; on alendronate since. [S]
Prednisone in the morning only; reduce salt and sweet drinks; walk daily.
Blood pressure at home twice a week; treat if it stays above 130/80 after the taper.
Stop atovaquone when prednisone falls below 20 mg.

At diagnosis, three months after starting treatment, then every three to six months while treatment changes
FVC 84 percent, FEV1 85 percent, FEV1/FVC 80 percent, DLCO 70 percent of predicted
Methotrexate safety: blood count, liver tests and creatinine
Before starting; every two to four weeks for the first three months; then every eight to twelve weeks

A deviation: the blood count, liver tests and creatinine due two to four weeks after methotrexate began were not done, because no laboratory order was placed for the long gap between visits. No harm resulted: today hemoglobin 13.1 g/dL, white cells 9.8 (raised by prednisone), lymphocytes 1.2, platelets 262, ALT 31, AST 28, alkaline phosphatase 96 U/L, albumin 4.1 g/dL, creatinine 0.92 mg/dL and eGFR 75 are normal. Corrective action: standing orders every four weeks until twelve weeks and then every eight to twelve weeks, at a laboratory near home or on tour, with a reminder to her and to the clinic

Follow-up: Methotrexate blood tests every four weeks. Remote device checks monthly. Review in mid-August after the repeat FDG-PET, echocardiogram and lung function. Call for fever, cough, breathlessness, a shock, or fainting. Next scheduled visit 1964-08-24: six months of treatment: repeat FDG-PET, steroid taper, and plans for touring. [S]
